questions.q: Why is the Schedule trigger set to 5 AM instead of closer to the 8 AM deadline?
options: To give real margin covering the source query, data flow startup, and any retries needed on a bad night
Because Data Factory can only trigger pipelines at 5 AM
It's arbitrary — the exact trigger time has no real effect
To ensure the pipeline runs before anyone else's system
questions.explain: Building in three hours of margin is a deliberate design choice, since a pipeline that only just barely makes the deadline on a good night has no room left for a bad one.

questions.q: What security treatment does the Azure SQL Database sink's credentials get, matching the source side?
options: A Key Vault reference, never a plain connection string
No credentials are needed for a sink connection
A hardcoded password directly in the pipeline JSON
Credentials stored in a plain text file in the Git repo
questions.explain: Closing out Lesson 53's security requirement means the sink gets the same Key Vault-referenced credential pattern as the source, not a plain connection string.

questions.q: What's the recommended RBAC split for this pipeline?
options: Data Factory Contributor only for the on-call team; Reader for everyone else who needs visibility
Contributor for every employee at Northwind
No RBAC is needed since the pipeline is automated
Owner role for all stakeholders who want to view pipeline status
questions.explain: Only the on-call data engineering team gets Contributor access to actually edit the pipeline; everyone else who needs visibility gets Reader, which allows monitoring without edit risk.

questions.q: What does the Log Analytics query in this lesson actually compute?
options: A 30-day success rate trend for this specific pipeline, summarized by day
The exact error message from the most recent failure only
The total number of datasets in the factory
A list of every linked service ever created
questions.explain: The query filters to this pipeline's runs over the last 30 days and summarizes a success rate percentage per day, turning "seems fine" into an actual verifiable trend.

questions.q: Why is the failed-activity-runs alert scoped specifically to this pipeline rather than left factory-wide?
options: A scoped alert stays meaningful; an unscoped one firing on any failure anywhere becomes noise people ignore
Scoping the alert makes it fire more frequently, which is desirable
Unscoped alerts aren't technically possible to configure
Scope has no effect on which failures trigger the alert
questions.explain: Consistent with Lesson 55's approach, scoping the alert to this one pipeline (rather than the whole factory) keeps it useful instead of becoming background noise.
